Vector code lost twice in this feature inside one instance and won here by a factor of two and a half, and the difference is only what a lane is: not a state, not a chunk, but a whole probe. "Scalar control, vector data" is what made it pay: the first lane walk loaded eight characters and classified them in vector code every step and cost 1.85 scalar steps; noticing that the lanes are at the same character 99 % of the time turned that into one table lookup and the scalar loop's own branches, at one scalar step. A generic step taxes the common case: making the walk charset-generic put a broadcast, an add and a counter into every step and took ASCII from 254 to 363 us until the charset became a type parameter. And a surviving mutant is sometimes the code's fault: the pair rule survived deletion because it was never needed.

**Benchmark delta.** Counted, work per plan as passes of the text (scalar program passes plus lane-walk steps): `mixed-40k-any` 7.00 → 1.00 + 2.00, digits then order lines 5.00 → 1.00 + 2.00, random runs 7.00 → 1.00 + 2.00, a Japanese mixture 7.00 → 1.00 + 2.00, a label-sized cap 7.83 → 2.00 + 2.01; short-chunk content and one-symbol texts unchanged. Planner alone, two launches: order lines 638 → 275 us (−57 %), random runs 506 → 217 (−57 %), digits then order lines 518 → 284 (−45 %), Japanese with numbers 507 → 192 (−62 %) and 398 → 130 (−67 %), Latin-1 with digits 170 → 75 (−56 %); the reuse alone −7 to −15 % on periodic content and within noise elsewhere. End to end, `QRCodeStructuredAppendEncode`, ShortRun, a worktree at the previous commit against this tree with the same benchmark file, three rounds alternating, `Optimal` arms: `mixed-40k-any` 1.88 / 1.95 / 1.83 → 1.44 / 1.40 / 1.45 ms (−24 %, Ratio 2.3x → 1.8x), `uneven-40k-any` 1.35 / 1.36 / 1.36 → 1.05 / 1.14 / 1.12 ms (−19 %), `utf8-15k-mixed` 1.16 / 1.16 / 1.14 → 0.89 / 0.86 / 0.85 ms (−25 %); the shapes whose searches run as `Single` and every `Single` arm within noise. Tried and not kept: budgets placed where balanced budgets cluster instead of evenly (it trades the second batch for scalar probes whose cost is the luck of the shared chunks: −35 % on one shape, +18 % on another), and a lane opening without the chunk-length condition (+23 to +56 % on 78-character chunks). What a plan costs now is one scalar pass and two batches, and none of the three yields to the same idea again; an ARM64 walk at four lanes of 128 bits is the open follow-up, since `Vector256` is not accelerated there.

### Performance round 14, the writer's plans taken together and only where they can differ (2026-09-18)

**Done.** The round was asked to hand the plan from the planner to the writer, so that a symbol is not planned a second time. That premise did not survive round 13: the split now comes out of a walk of eight budgets at once that carries costs only, so there is no last scalar walk to record predecessors in, and recording them in the lanes costs what it would save. What the planner can hand over is smaller and free, and the rest of the round went into the writer itself, after a table of its stages showed it at 200 us of a 1.45 ms set on order lines (the program with predecessors 110, the walk back over the table 49, two measurements 18, the segmented stream 30), twice the one pass the brief assumed, against 7 us for the single-mode stream of the same chunks. Shipped: the planner's existing pass for the longest dense runs also says when every plan is one Byte run (no run of digits reaching three, no alphanumeric run reaching six), and the Byte chunks of such a text are written as their single-mode stream with no program run; the plan builder hands its measurement to its caller, and the relocated-BOM check, the unit counts and the measurement are one pass over the runs; the program with predecessors carries its states as keys (cost shifted up three bits over the state's number), so the predecessor is the low bits of the minimum the cost-only loop takes anyway; the table is two bytes a character instead of seven, for all three symbologies, and the walk back goes run by run, reading only the places a run can begin; and the plans of up to eight symbols of a set are taken in one pass, a vector lane each (`ModeSegmenter.Lanes.cs`, .NET 8 and later, portable `Vector256`), only symbols that take a plan getting a lane. `StructuredAppendWriterPlanTest` holds the lanes to the plan each chunk builds alone (seven ways of cutting, three bands, a table full of noise), the verdict to every chunk it is said about and to not being said at three digits, the set under the verdict to the single-mode set, and the set to the same modules with and without the lanes; four planted faults were all caught. The same program built against the previous commit and this tree emits identical modules over 4,392 encodes through the public API (1,392 Structured Append settings; 3,000 single symbols in each of Standard QR, rMQR and Micro QR, whose plans the shared program also writes).

**Lessons.** A brief carries the design it was written under: "hand over the last walk's plan" named a walk the round before had removed, and the way to find that out was to read the code as it stands and measure its stages before designing anything. The stage table also doubled the estimate; the program was the visible cost and the walk back, which nobody had looked at, was close to half of it. A dependent load is not removed by replacing it with arithmetic of the same depth (decoding the state from a packed word was slower than the load); it is removed by making the address not depend on anything, and the structure of the packing groups gave that and a third of the steps besides. A rewrite that only draws in scalar code can still be the one to keep: the keyed minimum is no faster than the ordered compare chains, since a minimum compiles to a branch either way, but it is what lets a vector lane take the minimum and have the tie-break and the predecessor fall out of it, which the chains would have cost fifteen compares and blends a step. End-to-end measurement found what no component test could: the first port gave every symbol a lane, chunks of digits included, which are never planned and as the longest lane kept the others waiting, and the all-digit shape lost 17 %. And an A/B is only as good as its two sides: the console probe built for a quieter number than the benchmark gives on this machine pointed both of its builds at the same tree, because a substitution in its project file silently did not match, and said "no gain" for an hour; timers planted in the library and read by reflection are what showed both sides running the new code. A comparison harness should print which tree it loaded.

**Benchmark delta.** The writer alone (chunk to data codewords, every chunk of the set, ratio to the previous code): order lines 0.38, digits then order lines 0.41, random runs 0.43, all alphanumeric 0.56, Japanese with numbers 0.52, prose 0.07, single symbols 0.75; its walk back 45 → 8 us and its program 110 → about 35 us on order lines. End to end, `QRCodeStructuredAppendEncode`, ShortRun, a worktree at the previous commit against this tree with the same benchmark file, three rounds alternating, `Optimal` arms, means: `mixed-40k-any` 1,467 → 1,322 us (−10 %), `uneven-40k-any` 1,130 → 996 (−12 %), `byte-45k-any` 1,326 → 1,165 (−12 %), `byte-45k-v40` −20 %, `byte-45k-boost` −14 %, `byte-4k-max10` 72 → 58 (−19 %), `utf8-15k-any` −4 %, `utf8-15k-mixed` −2 % (one noisy round; −8 % in the pinned probe), `numeric-100k-any` +1 %; the `Single` arms, which this round does not touch, moved between −5 % and +2 %, which is the noise of this machine today. A console probe through the public API, pinned to a core at high priority, minimum of 300 after a warm-up, three rounds alternating, agrees: `mixed-40k-any` 1,455 → 1,319 us (−9 %), `uneven-40k-any` 1,084 → 1,009 (−7 %), `utf8-15k-mixed` 958 → 882 (−8 %), `byte-45k-any` 1,331 → 1,210 (−9 %), `byte-4k-max10` 73 → 60 (−18 %), `numeric-100k-any` unchanged, every `Single` arm within 2 %. What is left of an `Optimal` set of order lines is about 250 us of planner and 950 us of symbols (error correction, placement, masking, the same work a `Single` set pays).
